question.text: The PFUTP Regulations provide that the list of acts or omissions in Regulation 4(2) is:

answer.text: Exhaustive for intermediaries but illustrative for non-intermediaries
Applicable only to registered market participants
Exhaustive and no other acts can be considered as fraudulent
Not exhaustive, and any act or omission is prohibited if it falls within the purview of Regulation 3

explanation.text: The Logic: The PFUTP Regulations expressly state that the acts and omissions listed in Regulation 4(2) are not exhaustive and that any act or omission is prohibited if it falls within the purview of Regulation 3, even if it is not specifically listed. The Trap: Option A is the false intermediaries/non-intermediaries distinction — the non-exhaustive nature applies equally to all. Option C wrongly treats the list as exhaustive, which contradicts the express clarification in the regulation. Note: Source-backed to NISM-Series-III-A workbook (Dec 2025), page 146.
